newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Telebras seen fundamentally strong despite plunge.
newsitem.headline: Telebras seen fundamentally strong despite plunge.

text.p: Federal telecom Telebras' market value plunged as Brazilian shares tumbled last week but the firm's fundamentals remain strong and its stock price is likely to rebound, analysts said.
"The company's fundamentals did not change one bit," said Marcelo Mollica, an analyst with local investment bank Banco Icatu.
"As privatization approaches, the stock price should improve," he added, referring to next year's scheduled break-up and selloff of Telebras.

The Sao Paulo bolsa's Bovespa index of 47 top shares fell 15 percent last week on fears of a devaluation, led by blue chips including benchmark Telebras, which accounted for 60 percent of total trade.

As a result, the total value of Telebras shares on the market fell to 42.3 billion reais ($39.2 billion) on Friday from 54 billion reais ($50 billion) a week earlier, according to the O Globo newspaper.
"The entire market went down so (investors saw) problems with the country's fundamentals not the company's," said Vera Rossi, a telecoms analyst with ING Barings in Brazil.
Still, the strong contraction in Telebras' market value may worry the government, which hopes to garner hefty premiums when it auctions off the firm piecemeal starting in early 1998.
But analysts said the government is still likely to reap whopping prices when it sells Telebras, beginning with long-distance firm Embratel and its Sao Paulo unit Telesp .
"Not only did fundamentals not change, things actually were looking better" before stock prices collapsed, Mollica said.

He cited the sale of B Band cellular concession for the Sao Paulo area for 2.6 billion reais, four times the base price, and Congress' speedy approval of Brazil's new telecoms law just days before stocks plummeted.

Analysts said Telebras was ripe for profit-taking after rising as high as 180 reais this year from 80 reais at the end of last year. "Any reason was an excuse to take profits," said another telecoms analyst who works for a foreign investment bank.
On Monday, the Sao Paulo bourse was virtually flat at 1512 local/1412 EDT. Telebras preferred stock was down 0.37 percent at 139.48 reais. Telebras' ADR was flat at $128-7/8.
At its current price, Telebras "is more attractive than its peers in Latin America," Mollica said.
Given the company's strong fundamentals, a fair price today would be $157 per ADR, added ING's Rossi, who maintains a June 1998 target price of $180 for Telebras.
Analysts said the stock should continue to appreciate over the long term but at a more gradual pace than in the first half of 1997.
